stories.title: Hackers Exploit Critical Cisco Expressway Flaw, Breach Four Devices and Reach Internal Network
stories.abstract: CISA has added four critical vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including flaws in VMware vCenter, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver, and Apache Roller. These vulnerabilities are currently being actively exploited in the wild, posing significant risks to enterprise environments.
stories.why: Active exploitation of these vulnerabilities allows attackers to bypass authentication, gain unauthorized access, or execute arbitrary code on critical infrastructure components.
stories.action: Patch VMware vCenter, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver, and Apache Roller to the latest vendor-provided versions.

stories.title: Everything Is a Web Application, Including Your Firewall
stories.abstract: Palo Alto Networks confirmed active exploitation of two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, affecting PAN-OS management interfaces. These flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution, enabling attackers to compromise exposed firewall management consoles.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities allow full system takeover via the management interface, and they are currently being exploited in the wild.
stories.action: Restrict management interface access to trusted networks and apply available vendor patches immediately.

stories.title: PHP Fixes 7 Critical Flaws, Including Bugs That Could Allow Remote Code Execution
stories.abstract: The PHP development team has released security updates addressing 18 vulnerabilities across all supported versions. These patches resolve several critical remote code execution flaws, including CVE-2026-115560, which could allow unauthenticated attackers to compromise server processes and execute arbitrary code.
stories.why: Critical RCE vulnerabilities in core server-side languages pose a high risk of full system compromise and unauthorized data access.
stories.action: Update all PHP installations to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Amazon says Chinese hackers used Cairn AI tool to discover apparent zero-day during attack on university
stories.abstract: State-sponsored actors linked to China are utilizing the open-source Cairn AI framework to automate reconnaissance and exploit development. Researchers observed the tool being deployed against academic institutions to identify and weaponize previously unknown vulnerabilities in specialized software.
stories.why: The integration of autonomous AI into exploit chains significantly lowers the barrier for attackers to discover and weaponize zero-day vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Critical VMware vCenter Zero-Day Flaw Lets Network Attackers Bypass Authentication
stories.abstract: Broadcom has released patches for a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in VMware vCenter Server. Threat actors linked to Chinese espionage operations have been actively exploiting this flaw as a zero-day since September to gain unauthorized access to virtual infrastructure management consoles.
stories.why: The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to compromise central management systems, granting them full control over virtualized environments and hosted workloads.
stories.action: Update all VMware vCenter Server instances to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: China attackers deployed AI agents that autonomously found and exploited a 0-day to take over a university server
stories.abstract: Amazon security researchers observed Chinese state-sponsored actors utilizing autonomous AI agents to identify and weaponize a zero-day vulnerability. These agents operated independently for nearly 24 hours, successfully compromising a university server without requiring manual intervention or human guidance during the exploitation process.
stories.why: This marks a significant shift in threat actor capabilities, where AI-driven automation accelerates the discovery and exploitation lifecycle of previously unknown vulnerabilities.

stories.title: WhatsApp Patches 3 Security Flaws, Including Android Bug Suspected of Use in Scams
stories.abstract: Meta patched a vulnerability in WhatsApp for Android, identified as CVE-2026-23871, involving improper validation of external ad-reply URLs. The flaw was discovered during internal investigations into scam campaigns that leveraged the issue to increase the perceived legitimacy of fraudulent messages.
stories.why: Exploitation of URL validation flaws can facilitate sophisticated social engineering and phishing attacks by bypassing standard security warnings.
stories.action: Update WhatsApp for Android to version 2.26.17.4 or later.

stories.title: Chase, Visa, Mastercard confirm third-party cyberattacks that may have exposed customers' info
stories.abstract: JPMorgan Chase notified customers that a third-party service provider suffered a cyberattack, resulting in the unauthorized exposure of personal and marketing data. The bank is currently working to assess the full scope of the incident and the specific information compromised.
stories.why: Third-party vendor breaches remain a primary vector for supply chain attacks, highlighting the necessity of rigorous vendor risk management and data access controls.

stories.title: JPMorgan, Visa, Mastercard Cite Third-Party Incidents Amid Data Leak
stories.abstract: The N0n ransomware group has published sensitive data allegedly belonging to customers of JPMorgan, Visa, and Mastercard. The financial institutions attribute the exposure to security failures at third-party service providers rather than direct breaches of their own internal systems.
stories.why: Third-party vendor risk remains a critical attack vector for financial institutions, highlighting the need for rigorous supply chain security and data oversight.

stories.title: New Unpatched Windows 0-Day FastUnlock Lets Someone Holding a Locked PC Run Programs on It
stories.abstract: A researcher disclosed a zero-day technique dubbed FastUnlock that permits unauthorized users with physical access to a locked Windows machine to execute programs. While the exploit bypasses the lock screen, it restricts the attacker to a low-privileged account rather than administrative access.
stories.why: Physical access bypasses allow unauthorized interaction with locked endpoints, potentially facilitating further exploitation or data exfiltration.

stories.title: European Commission scrambles to contain AI-assisted cyberattack
stories.abstract: The European Commission experienced a targeted cyberattack that forced the suspension of internal HR and medical reimbursement systems. Officials are currently investigating the incident, which reportedly utilized AI-driven tools, though there is no current evidence that sensitive personal information was compromised.
stories.why: The use of AI-assisted tooling in targeted attacks against high-profile government infrastructure highlights evolving adversary capabilities and potential risks to internal administrative systems.

stories.title: Siemens Industrial Software Products
stories.abstract: Siemens has identified that several industrial software products are vulnerable to the Node2Shell flaw (CVE-2026-111497). This critical out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the bundled Node.js Brotli decoder could allow remote attackers to corrupt memory or execute arbitrary code on affected systems.
stories.why: This vulnerability is actively exploited and poses a significant risk of remote code execution within industrial environments.
stories.action: Review Siemens security bulletins and update affected software to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Hackers Exploiting Critical Puppet RCE Flaw Affecting Enterprise Management Servers
stories.abstract: CISA has added a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Perforce Puppet to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-115731, is currently being leveraged by attackers to compromise enterprise infrastructure management servers.
stories.why: Successful exploitation allows unauthorized actors to gain full control over configuration management systems, potentially leading to widespread infrastructure compromise.
stories.action: Patch all Perforce Puppet instances immediately.

stories.title: N-able says recent security breach led to major service outage
stories.abstract: N-able confirmed that a security breach on one of its servers triggered a global outage for its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud platforms. The company is investigating the incident, which potentially exposed user credentials.
stories.why: Service providers are high-value targets for supply chain attacks, and credential theft within these platforms can facilitate downstream compromises for managed service providers.

stories.title: Oracle to Patch 11 Java Flaws Today as Critical OpenJDK RCE (CVE-2026-114938) Report Emerges
stories.abstract: A critical heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability, identified as CVE-2026-114938 and nicknamed Java4Shell, affects the Base64 library in OpenJDK. This flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on systems running vulnerable Java runtimes.
stories.why: The vulnerability enables remote code execution in widely deployed Java environments, posing a significant risk to enterprise infrastructure and application security.
stories.action: Apply the latest OpenJDK security patches provided by your vendor immediately.

stories.title: TfL takes Oyster photocard website offline after attackers compromise customer accounts
stories.abstract: Transport for London confirmed a security incident involving its Oyster photocard system, potentially exposing the personal account information of approximately 265,000 customers. The breach was identified after unauthorized emails were distributed to users through the agency's internal messaging infrastructure.
stories.why: This incident highlights the risk of supply chain or internal system compromise leading to unauthorized data access and potential phishing campaigns against users.

stories.title: Hackers steal data of 1.6 million SBC Medical Group customers
stories.abstract: SBC Medical Group disclosed two separate security incidents resulting in the unauthorized exposure of sensitive personal data belonging to approximately 1.6 million individuals. The breaches affected databases containing information on both patients and employees associated with the organization's Japanese clinics.
stories.why: Large-scale exposure of PII increases the risk of targeted phishing and identity theft for affected individuals, potentially impacting organizational reputation and regulatory compliance.

stories.title: Linux KVM Flaw CVE-2026-99312 Lets Guest VMs Access Host Memory on AMD Hosts
stories.abstract: A vulnerability in the Linux KVM hypervisor allows guest virtual machines on AMD-based systems to access host memory. By exploiting this flaw, attackers with control over a guest VM can potentially read sensitive data belonging to the host or other co-resident virtual machines.
stories.why: This represents a critical isolation failure in multi-tenant cloud environments, enabling cross-tenant data exfiltration on affected AMD hardware.
stories.action: Update Linux kernel to the latest patched version.

stories.title: SAP security advisory – November 2025 monthly rollup (AV25-738) – Update 1
stories.abstract: SAP released a comprehensive set of security patches for November 2025, covering a wide range of enterprise products including HANA, NetWeaver, Solution Manager, and various client-side components. These updates address multiple vulnerabilities across the vendor's software ecosystem.
stories.why: Unpatched SAP vulnerabilities often provide high-value targets for attackers seeking unauthorized access to sensitive enterprise data and core business processes.
stories.action: Review the SAP security portal and apply the latest patches for your specific product versions.

stories.title: [Control Systems] Moxa security advisory (AV26-1187)
stories.abstract: Moxa has disclosed multiple critical vulnerabilities affecting a wide range of industrial networking hardware, including the ioLogik E1200 series and several Ethernet switch product lines. These flaws include buffer overflows and other security weaknesses that could potentially be exploited by remote attackers.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities impact critical industrial control infrastructure, potentially allowing unauthorized code execution or system compromise in operational technology environments.
stories.action: Review Moxa security advisories and apply firmware updates for affected devices as they become available.

stories.title: Bell Canada says 'agentic' hacker stole enterprise customer data
stories.abstract: Bell Canada reported a security breach involving an automated, agentic threat actor that accessed its internal systems on November 17, 2026. The unauthorized party successfully exfiltrated enterprise customer data, specifically targeting information related to telecommunications circuit provisioning and ordering processes.
stories.why: The use of agentic AI-driven tools by attackers signals an evolution in automated exploitation capabilities against enterprise infrastructure.

stories.title: Black Hat USA 2026 | GPUBreach: Privilege Escalation Attacks on GPUs Using Rowhammer
stories.abstract: Researchers developed GPUBreach, a technique demonstrating that Rowhammer attacks on NVIDIA GPUs can move beyond simple data corruption. By reverse engineering page table allocation, attackers can induce deterministic bit flips to achieve privilege escalation and unauthorized cross-process memory access.
stories.why: This research proves that GPU-based memory corruption can lead to full-system compromise, challenging the assumption that GPU bit flips only affect model accuracy.

stories.title: Drupal security advisory (AV26-1186)
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities have been disclosed affecting Drupal core, Mitel MiCollab, and various PHP versions. These flaws include potential remote code execution risks, necessitating immediate attention from administrators to secure their respective environments against exploitation.
stories.why: Unpatched RCE vulnerabilities in core web infrastructure and communication platforms present high-risk entry points for unauthorized system access and data compromise.
stories.action: Update Drupal to 10.6.22, 11.3.22, or 11.4.13; update PHP and Mitel MiCollab to the latest patched versions.

stories.title: Still tracking company passwords in spreadsheets? You’re flying blind.
stories.abstract: Storing corporate credentials in spreadsheets creates significant security gaps, leaving administrators unable to monitor for weak, recycled, or leaked passwords. Transitioning to centralized management platforms provides better visibility into credential health and enforces safer sharing practices across the organization.
stories.why: Unmanaged credentials in plaintext files are prime targets for attackers and prevent effective oversight of organizational security posture.

stories.title: Ruby Patches Ruby2Shell Vulnerability That Could Lead to RCE
stories.abstract: The Ruby programming language maintainers have released a security update to address CVE-2026-132825, a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability. If exploited, this flaw could allow an attacker to achieve remote code execution on affected systems.
stories.why: Remote code execution vulnerabilities in core language runtimes pose a critical risk to any application infrastructure relying on the affected Ruby versions.
stories.action: Update your Ruby installation to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Scans for LiteLLM/Starlette (CVE-2026-42271, CVE-2026-48710), (Mon, Nov 16th)
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively scanning for vulnerabilities in LiteLLM and Starlette, specifically targeting endpoints associated with CVE-2026-42271 and CVE-2026-48710. These flaws can be chained to facilitate unauthenticated remote code execution.
stories.why: Exploitation allows attackers to gain full system control without authentication, posing a critical risk to infrastructure running these frameworks.
stories.action: Patch LiteLLM and Starlette installations immediately to the latest secure versions.

stories.title: F5 releases emergency patches for critical BIG-IP RCE flaws
stories.abstract: F5 has issued urgent security updates for its BIG-IP platform to remediate five critical vulnerabilities. These flaws could allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or trigger denial-of-service conditions, potentially compromising the availability and integrity of affected network infrastructure.
stories.why: Critical RCE vulnerabilities in edge networking appliances are primary targets for initial access and lateral movement within enterprise environments.
stories.action: Update BIG-IP software to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: phpAfterShell Explained: How Hackers Could Turn a PHP Session Flaw Into Code Execution
stories.abstract: A race condition in PHP's default session handling allows attackers to manipulate session files during write operations. By injecting malicious objects, adversaries can trigger remote code execution if the application environment contains compatible gadget chains.
stories.why: This vulnerability enables unauthenticated remote code execution, posing a critical risk to any PHP-based application relying on default session storage.
stories.action: Update PHP to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: How to Tell If It’s a Cyberattack or Just an Outage
stories.abstract: Recent high-profile service disruptions across critical infrastructure have fueled speculation regarding cyberattacks. Security analysts emphasize that most widespread outages stem from technical errors, configuration mistakes, or infrastructure failures rather than malicious digital interference, urging organizations to avoid jumping to conclusions during incidents.
stories.why: Misattributing technical failures to cyberattacks leads to poor incident response, wasted resources, and unnecessary panic during critical downtime.

stories.title: Autonomy Logic OpenPLC Runtime
stories.abstract: A race condition in Autonomy Logic OpenPLC Runtime versions 4.2.4 and earlier allows attackers to bypass existence checks. By sending concurrent requests, unauthorized users can create multiple administrative accounts within the system.
stories.why: This flaw enables unauthorized privilege escalation in industrial control environments, potentially granting attackers full administrative control over critical infrastructure systems.
stories.action: Update Autonomy Logic OpenPLC Runtime to a version beyond 4.2.4.

stories.title: Elecbrakes EB2, VM1, ELBC2000
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in Elecbrakes EB2, VM1, and ELBC2000 trailer brake controllers allow attackers to bypass authentication, modify firmware, and manipulate safety-critical functions, including brake operation and lighting systems.
stories.why: Exploitation could lead to physical safety hazards and loss of control over vehicle braking systems.
stories.action: Update EB2 to version 3.0.4.2.1 or later and VM1 to version 1.3.4.2.1 or later.

stories.title: libumqtt
stories.abstract: The libumqtt library, versions 1.1.1 and earlier, contains an integer underflow vulnerability. Remote attackers can exploit this flaw to trigger memory corruption, disclose sensitive information, or crash the application through a denial-of-service condition.
stories.why: This library is utilized across critical infrastructure sectors, and the vulnerability allows for remote exploitation with significant impact on system stability and data integrity.

stories.title: Container Store restores systems after cyberattack
stories.abstract: The Container Store successfully brought its online platforms and internal infrastructure back online following a security breach that occurred over the weekend. Parent company Neighborhood Intelligence confirmed the restoration of services but provided no further details regarding the nature of the incident.
stories.why: Retailers remain high-value targets for data theft; understanding the scope of such incidents is critical for assessing potential exposure of customer information.

stories.title: Java and NGINX Security Bugs, a Week of Outages, and the Optimizely Hack
stories.abstract: Recent vulnerabilities dubbed Java4Shell and NGINX2Root have emerged, alongside a supply chain incident where Optimizely's A/B testing scripts were compromised to distribute malware. These events highlight ongoing risks in widely deployed infrastructure components and third-party script integrations.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities impact ubiquitous enterprise software, while the Optimizely incident demonstrates how trusted third-party scripts can be weaponized for malware delivery.
stories.action: Review Cloudflare's Java4Shell WAF guidance and audit third-party script inclusions for potential supply chain compromise.

stories.title: 10-Year-Old NGINX HTTP/2 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code on Servers
stories.abstract: A decade-old vulnerability, CVE-2026-123007, has been identified in NGINX's HTTP/2 implementation. This flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code within the context of the NGINX worker process. Patches are available in versions 1.31.9 and 1.30.7.
stories.why: Remote code execution in a core web server component poses a critical risk to infrastructure integrity and data confidentiality.
stories.action: Update NGINX to version 1.31.9 or 1.30.7 immediately.

stories.title: Ransomware Recovery Takes 20 Days for the Typical Victim, Report Finds
stories.abstract: A recent study indicates that organizations hit by ransomware require a median of 20 days to restore operations. Nearly one-third of these victims struggle with recovery processes that extend beyond six weeks, highlighting significant operational downtime following a successful attack.
stories.why: Extended recovery timelines demonstrate that current backup and disaster recovery strategies are often insufficient to meet business continuity requirements during major incidents.

stories.title: UAT-12643: Suspected North Korea-aligned actor blends blockchain resilience with targeted infostealing
stories.abstract: A North Korean-linked threat actor, identified as UAT-12643, is utilizing the Solana blockchain to mask command-and-control communications. The group employs a remote access trojan that maintains persistence on Windows systems even after a factory reset.
stories.why: This technique demonstrates an evolving trend of using decentralized ledgers to obfuscate malicious traffic and evade traditional network-based detection methods.

stories.title: Five warning signs of ransomware breach before encryption or data theft
stories.abstract: Security researchers have identified five key indicators of compromise that typically precede ransomware deployment. These early warning signs include unauthorized credential harvesting, lateral network movement, and deliberate efforts by attackers to neutralize security software before data exfiltration or encryption occurs.
stories.why: Recognizing these pre-encryption behaviors allows security teams to disrupt the attack chain before the most destructive phases of a ransomware incident take place.

stories.title: Java4Shell Flaw (CVE-2026-114938) Enables Pre-Auth RCE in Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak and More
stories.abstract: A critical memory-corruption vulnerability, CVE-2026-114938, affects OpenJDK versions 17.0.6 and later. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution on x86-64 systems utilizing AVX-512 VBMI instructions, impacting major enterprise software like Jira, Jenkins, and Keycloak.
stories.why: This vulnerability enables unauthenticated RCE on critical infrastructure and widely deployed enterprise applications, posing a significant risk to internal network security.
stories.action: Update OpenJDK to the latest patched version immediately, prioritizing internet-facing applications.

stories.title: To Catch a Ransomware Scammer, FBI Posed as Both Victim and Attacker
stories.abstract: Federal agents successfully apprehended an alleged fraudster by orchestrating a sting operation where they simultaneously impersonated both the targeted ransomware victim and the malicious actors involved in the extortion attempt.
stories.why: This highlights sophisticated law enforcement tactics in disrupting cybercrime syndicates through active deception and infrastructure infiltration.

stories.title: Nvidia adds possible hack to list of very bad things under investigation
stories.abstract: Nvidia is currently investigating a potential data breach after a ransomware syndicate threatened to publish sensitive corporate information. The threat actors have issued an ultimatum, demanding payment to prevent the unauthorized release of the company's internal files.
stories.why: Large-scale data exfiltration from major hardware manufacturers often exposes intellectual property, supply chain vulnerabilities, and sensitive employee or customer records.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Friday, November 20th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10188, (Fri, Nov 20th)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center's daily podcast provides a summary of current cybersecurity events, threat intelligence, and technical analysis relevant to security practitioners for November 20th, 2026.
stories.why: Staying informed on daily threat trends and emerging vulnerabilities is essential for maintaining situational awareness in enterprise security operations.

stories.title: F5 security advisory (AV26-1178)
stories.abstract: F5 has released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across its BIG-IP product line, including BIG-IP, APM, SSL Orchestrator, PEM, CNF, and BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes. Affected versions require specific engineering hotfixes to mitigate potential security risks.
stories.why: F5 appliances are critical infrastructure gateways; unpatched vulnerabilities here often provide attackers with high-privilege access to internal network traffic and authentication flows.
stories.action: Update BIG-IP, CNF, and Next for Kubernetes instances to the specified patched versions immediately.

stories.title: CISA Warns of 4 Exploited Flaws Linked to Ransomware, Cryptomining, and LLMjacking Attacks
stories.abstract: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to include four security flaws affecting Synology DSM, BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis, and REDCap. These vulnerabilities are currently being leveraged by threat actors for ransomware, cryptomining, and unauthorized LLM access.
stories.why: Active exploitation of these specific services indicates they are high-value targets for attackers seeking initial access or resource theft.
stories.action: Review CISA KEV catalog and patch Synology, LiteLLM, Apache Axis, and REDCap instances immediately.

stories.title: In Other News: Norwegian Energy Firm Cyberattacks, Supercomputer Hack, New Nightmare Eclipse Exploit
stories.abstract: The European Union has sanctioned the NoName057(16) hacktivist group. Meanwhile, researchers identified malware campaigns targeting common access cards on personal devices, and reports indicate that Gemini agents were utilized to compromise Epoch AI systems.
stories.why: These incidents highlight evolving threats to supply chains, authentication hardware, and the security of AI-driven research environments.

stories.title: Bazuka Android Malware Uses Fake Screen Overlays to Hide Credential Theft and Device Control
stories.abstract: Researchers identified Bazuka, a sophisticated Android malware framework utilizing LLM-driven automation to manage infected devices. The threat, discovered during an investigation into NFC-relay banking Trojans, enables large-scale credential theft and remote device control through deceptive screen overlays.
stories.why: The integration of LLMs into mobile malware frameworks suggests a shift toward more efficient, automated, and scalable victim management for threat actors.

stories.title: Podcast: I Spoke to an AI Fraud Kingpin
stories.abstract: A recent investigative report explores the operations of OnlyFake, a service utilizing artificial intelligence to generate sophisticated fraudulent identification documents. The discussion highlights the evolving landscape of synthetic identity theft and the challenges posed by AI-driven document forgery.
stories.why: AI-generated identity verification bypasses traditional KYC and authentication controls, posing a significant threat to identity assurance and fraud prevention systems.

stories.title: SonicWall Warns Gen 6 Firewalls Won't Get Security Patches, Even for Critical Flaws
stories.abstract: SonicWall has officially ended support for its Generation 6 firewalls. The company warns that these legacy devices are no longer receiving security updates and are highly vulnerable to automated, AI-driven exploitation if left exposed to the internet.
stories.why: Unpatched edge devices are primary targets for initial access, and these units will remain permanently vulnerable to all future discovered flaws.
stories.action: Decommission and replace all Generation 6 firewalls immediately.

stories.title: Russian COLD RELIC Hackers Use Stolen Google Workspace Data to Breach Second U.S. Organization
stories.abstract: The Russian-linked threat actor Cold Relic is exploiting data harvested from initial cloud environment breaches to facilitate secondary attacks. By leveraging stolen information for highly tailored social engineering and impersonation, the group successfully pivots from one victim to compromise additional third-party targets.
stories.why: This demonstrates a sophisticated supply chain pivot strategy where attackers weaponize internal communications and data to bypass trust-based security controls.

stories.title: Second Norwegian Energy Company Breached in 2 Days
stories.abstract: Two separate Norwegian energy firms have suffered security breaches within a forty-eight-hour window. While investigators have not confirmed a direct connection between the incidents, the operational similarities suggest a coordinated or thematic campaign targeting the region's critical infrastructure sector.
stories.why: Energy sector entities are high-value targets for state-sponsored actors seeking to map or disrupt critical industrial control systems.
